items.item: The full-refresh measurement is taken both before and after an identical small change, isolating change size as the variable that does not move the cost, rather than asserting insensitivity abstractly

at.step: Reveal: this topic's own measured result — full refresh is flat

items.item: The incremental-maintenance measurement uses a genuinely separate trigger-maintained table rather than PostgreSQL's REFRESH, since PostgreSQL has no built-in incremental materialized view refresh — the trigger stands in honestly for the mechanism, not disguised as a native feature

at.step: Reveal: this topic's own measured incremental-maintenance result

items.item: The CONCURRENTLY measurement uses two real concurrent sessions against the same materialized view, not a simulated or estimated contrast

The floating-point and staleness-bound claims are explicitly disclosed as sourced-only, consistent with this chapter's honest-gap pattern, rather than silently presented with the same confidence as the measured claims
DBSP and differential dataflow are named as the formalism behind the trigger-style mechanism this topic actually measures, not introduced as a disconnected buzzword
A closing check that requires reasoning about blocking behavior under CONCURRENTLY directly, rather than re-testing the exact measured millisecond figures from the reveals
The recap keeps full-refresh cost, incremental cost, and the CONCURRENTLY locking tradeoff as three separate ideas rather than one vague 'materialized views are good' takeaway
